samples.summary: The new shell behavior (case default, redirect-not-pipe, exit-1-without-verdict ⇒ crash) is only asserted as YAML TEXT — no test ever executes the block, so the actual branch behavior is unverified
samples.evidence: All coverage of the behavior change is `assert.match(window, /.../)` against the raw workflow string (lines 343-387). Nothing spawns `bash` with the extracted block and a stub `mark-ready` returning 0/1-with-verdict/1-without-verdict/2/3/127, so a syntactically-matching but behaviorally-wrong block (e.g. `grep` on a path that differs from the redirect target, `$RUNNER_TEMP` unset, a `case` pattern order that shadows, `set -e` interaction) passes. The todo file confirms the six-status check was done by hand ("was extracted and simulated", line 92-95) and not captured as a test. The one genuinely executed cross-file assertion is only the grep needle vs. mark-ready stdout (lines 389-398).

samples.summary: `ghMutate`'s fallback branch (GH_MUTATION_TOKEN unset ⇒ use the default gh token) has no test; run() now always sets both tokens
samples.evidence: mark-ready.mjs:93-97 has two branches; every `run()` call passes GH_MUTATION_TOKEN: APP_TOKEN (test line 120), so the `: process.env` fallback used by local dry runs is never exercised. Deleting it (or making it throw when the var is unset) would leave the whole suite green.

samples.summary: The token test only covers the happy promote path; the exit-3 path's `pr ready` credential and the label re-read's credential are not asserted
samples.evidence: The token assertions run a single `run(["7", "--promote"])` with all gates green (line 276). The exit-3 scenario (line 297) reads only `calls`, never `tokenCalls`, so a regression that sent the failing `pr ready` with the wrong credential — the exact 'Resource not accessible by integration' failure the override exists for — would be invisible there.

samples.summary: Window-based YAML assertions are loosely bounded: `esac` and `case "$code" in` are matched anywhere in a 2600-char slice that can spill into following steps
samples.evidence: `const window = yml.slice(at, at + 2600)` (line 338) then `assert.match(window, /^\s*esac$/m)` (372) — the closing `esac` is not tied to the `case` under test, and the magic 2600 must be re-tuned whenever nearby YAML grows, a maintenance hazard the earlier 1200 already showed.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. mark-ready.test.mjs:329-399 asserts against the real .github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml: it requires `> "$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log" 2>&1` (:359), `case "$code" in` (:363), the 0/2/3 arms (:364-366), the `*)` default (:369), `esac` (:372) and a `1)` arm doing `grep -qF ... mark-ready.log` (:377-382). The workflow in the working tree at agent-review-panel.yml:1494-1504 still has the old four-`if` chain with no redirect, no case, no default and no grep, so those assertions cannot pass on this branch. The workflow half sits unapplied in docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-workflow.patch (lines 15/24/29/39/46 add exactly the missing constructs), and docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:55-91 states the test "fails on purpose ... 13/14 without it" pending an out-of-band `git apply`. The test has no skip/todo/conditional guard and is picked up by the lane runner scripts/agent/package.json:8 (`node --test '**/*.test.mjs'`), so the scripts/agent lane ships red and masks other regressions there. Real and blocking under the test-adequacy rubric (coverage presented for a behavior change that cannot execute/pass).

verdict.reason: The factual core of the claim is accurate — I searched repo-wide (grep for `mark-ready.log`, `case "$code"`, `unhandled status`, and every `bash`/`/bin/bash` spawn in *.test.mjs, plus scripts/test/*) and no test extracts and executes the promote shell block; the only bash-spawning tests (ask/harvest/hunt-gate/collect-captures) are unrelated. But it is not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric. (1) The coverage is demonstrably non-vacuous: the working-tree workflow still carries the OLD `if` chain (agent-review-panel.yml:1499-1504), so `assert.match(window, /case "$code" in/)` at mark-ready.test.mjs:363 FAILS right now — assertions that fail when the behavior is absent are the opposite of fake coverage. (2) The specific escapes the finding names are in fact pinned: redirect target and grep target are asserted against the same literal `"$RUNNER_TEMP/mark-ready.log"` (359, 380), so a path mismatch cannot pass; `code=$?` existence is asserted before use as a slice bound (356-357); pipe-vs-redirect is asserted (360); the `1)` branch must grep AND `exit 2; }` and is forbidden a command-position `exit 0/1/3` (381-387). (3) The one truly leak-prone coupling — the grep needle vs. mark-ready's real stdout — IS executed (389-398), and 0/1/2/3 script-side behavior is exercised by running the real CLI as a process with a stub `gh` (102-136), nothing mocked away. (4) Regex-on-YAML is the established convention for workflow shape in this repo (score-all.test.mjs:901, replay-plan.test.mjs:579-584, pick-fix-credential.test.mjs:172-173, loop-status.test.mjs:442); treating it as blocking would condemn all of them. A bash-harness simulation of the six statuses would be a real improvement (the todo says it was done by hand, lines 92-95) but that is "coverage could be broader" = minor, not "a behavior change with no meaningful test at all", and the rubric tells me not to blocker-flag "add more tests" when meaningful falsifiable coverage exists.
